notes: Costs never change a trade's path in the frozen rule (the stop and the exit are price-based), so every figure here is the same set of trades re-costed; n does not move with x.

The gross edge is +0.261R a trade on USD/JPY 2016-now with a median stop of 19.5 pips, so each pip a round trip costs about 0.051R at the median (the mean of 1 / D is what counts: shorter stops pay more in R).

How to measure the missing figure: read bid / ask of USD/JPY and the four crosses at 00:55 and 06:00 UTC on real gotobi mornings (the price stream already carries both sides; a demo account with the yen pairs would add the broker's own quote and fills). topics.headline: NOT CAPTURABLE. Read on the strict fill rule as pre-registered: E1 k=2 strict keeps 5.4 % of E3's net R per day (+0.0080R against +0.1481R), month t +0.24, filling 54.5 % of days.

notes: The fill rules are on M1 highs: a high may have lasted a moment and a real queue may not have reached the order, so even the strict rule (0.3 pip through) is an estimate, not a measured broker fill. Mid prices: a real sell limit fills on the bid, about half a spread lower.

A fill is credited at the limit price even when the candle opened above it (no price improvement), and a stop reached inside the fill candle counts as stopped (the order inside the candle is unknown). Both are the worse case.
The frozen costs (spread plus 0.5 pip slippage a side) are charged on the limit fills too: no rebate is taken for a resting order.

What the misses cost: on the days E1 k=0 strict did not fill, E3 made +0.2138R a trade; on the days it filled, E3 made +0.1357R. A limit above the market fills on the days the price ticks up into the fix, which are not a random half of the days.

Read after the reading, descriptive only: most fills come in the 00:54 candle, before the fix minute. The 00:55 open sits on average +0.29 pips from the 00:53 close (median +0.20, above it on 52.1 % of days), and E2 (00:54 market) already loses about half of E3. A limit near the 00:53 close sells at roughly the 00:54 price, not the 00:55 one; a higher limit fills less often and misses days E3 made money on.
Month t on per-day net R is a measure of noise, not a test: no Holm, no placebo. Nothing here is chosen; any live use would need its own proposal and the owner.

Known before the study and said in the pre-registration: #878's M5 run already showed the fade on every non-gotobi day of 2016-now at −0.0628R a trade (n 1,870, month t −2.37). The M1 figure here is −0.0629R (n 1870).

T2 is a minute move in pips, not a trade: no cost applies. Its Welch t treats every day as independent; days are about a day apart and a one-minute move has little autocorrelation, so this is the plain reading the pre-registration fixed.

Read after the verdict, descriptive and not tested (the pre-registration named the minute after the fix as descriptive only): in 2016-now the minute INTO the fix rises about the same on both kinds of day (gotobi +0.332 pips, other days +0.379), while the minute AFTER it falls −1.336 pips on gotobi days against −0.187 on other days. So the gotobi difference, if it is real, is in the fall after 09:55, not in the rise before it; a test of that needs its own pre-registration on other data.

The placebo is reported, not part of the reading: it shows whether the fix minute on ordinary days stands out from ordinary minutes of the same morning (a one-minute move into a 5-minute mark), and whether the 00:55 sell on ordinary days beats a sell at an ordinary mark of the morning.

No live proposal: this study only describes where the gotobi fade's effect comes from. Whether the gotobi fade itself is ever traded is an owner decision outside it, and the timing study (#908) already showed it needs a fill at the 00:55:00 price.
